Hi Elena — answering your ask with a compact recommendation below. Attachments: ramsey_hosting_comparison_slide.pdf, ramsey_gpu_slate.xlsx (detailed counts and monthly TCO).

Executive summary (short):
- Private (VPC / air-gapped): recommended if Ramsey requires strict custody + on-premise-only data residency. Higher up-front engineering & ops overhead; best for regulatory/regulator-facing evidence. For POC we recommend a small private cluster that mirrors production topology to avoid migration risk.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): lower ops burden, faster time-to-value, Redwood manages the control plane and patching. Good SLA and predictable throughput; supports strict network isolation via VPC peering and private endpoints in many cases.

Sizing recommendation (POC -> Prod conservative path):
- POC (4–8 weeks): Dedicated baseline: 4xA100-80GB equivalent (concurrency target 20 qps sustained, headroom to 150 qps bursts with autoscale/burst). Private baseline: 6xA100 (to preserve headroom + no multi-tenant burst).
- Production ramp (steady-state): Dedicated commit: 12xA100 baseline with burst capacity to 24x; Private commit: 24xA100 cluster(s) with optional warm standby nodes.

Key tradeoffs and procurement impact:
- Lead times: Private (on-prem or private VPC dedicated racks) typically adds procurement lead time and possible hardware lease agreements — expect 6–12 weeks for dedicated hardware provisioning in a VPC/air-gapped model vs 2–4 weeks for Reserved Dedicated capacity from Redwood.
- SLAs & Credits: Dedicated reserved pools come with SLA guarantees and credits (negotiable above standard tiers); Private deployments require custom enterprise terms.
- Cost: Private has higher fixed monthly infrastructure amortization and possible setup fees. Dedicated reserved pricing yields lower marginal cost per token at mid/large scale because Redwood optimizes GPU placement and sharing for non-conflicting workloads. See attached XLS for line-item math.

Recommended path for Ramsey (practical):
1) Run POC on Dedicated reserved pool to validate prompts, evals, and data flow (2–4 weeks).
2) If regulator requires custody or air-gapping, plan a migration to Private with a canary cluster that mirrors the POC for compliance demos; parallel-run for 2 weeks before cutover.

Deliverables included: one-slide comparison, GPU slate + TCO (xlsx). Will follow up with an ops checklist and a sample procurement clause for Private licensing.

Thanks,
Marissa

Elena / team — quick technical sizing notes to complement Marissa’s summary. Attaching a quick workload-profile CSV with the math.

Assumptions used (conservative):
- Avg tokens per request: 350 (prompt+response).
- Average generation throughput per A100-80GB @ Redwood runtime (quantized medium): ~180–220 tokens/sec sustained. Using 200 tok/s for estimates.
- Effective concurrency target for 25 qps (avg) => ~25 concurrent generations, headroom for bursts to 150 qps translates to 150 concurrent if bursts fully parallelized. We size for 2x sustained concurrency to avoid queuing.

Sizing bullets:
- Dedicated 4xA100 (POC): supports sustained ~50 concurrent streams (~10–12 qps for heavy-token workloads) — adequate for initial validations with autoscale to burst nodes. We recommend enabling prefix/KV cache to reduce tokens per call for repeated context.
- Private 6xA100 (POC): because no shared burst options, reserve additional nodes to avoid cold-start tail latency for KV-heavy workloads.
- Production: target 12xA100 (dedicated reserved) for predictable mid-volume; add burst pool + autoscaler to handle scheduled peaks. Private should provision ~24xA100 (or partitioned clusters) to achieve the same headroom without cross-tenant burst.

Operational notes:
- Cold-starts and KV cache priming are the dominant latency risks for Private clusters. Consider warm-up jobs and managed KV pre-loading.
- If Ramsey needs guaranteed 200ms p99 for all requests, we suggest an SLA runway with canary traffic for 2 weeks and an SLO-based credit schedule in the contract.

Attachments: workload_profile_estimates.csv (CSV) — this includes token math, model variants, and a recommended autoscale policy (min/max nodes, scale step).

Happy to walk through the CSV on a short call.

-Karthik
